verses.1: In you, LORD, I have taken refuge. Let me never be put to shame.
verses.2: In your righteousness, rescue me and deliver me. Incline your ear to me and save me.
verses.3: Be to me a rock of refuge, a fortress where I can always run for safety. You have commanded to save me, for you are my rock and my stronghold.
verses.4: My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the deceitful and cruel.
verses.5: For you are my hope, LORD my God, my trust from my youth.
verses.6: I have relied on you since birth, from the womb you have been my refuge. In you my praise has been ever constant.
verses.7: I have been like a wonder to many, but you are my mighty Helper.
verses.8: My mouth will be filled with your praise. I will sing your glory all the day, your majesty.
verses.9: Do not cast me away in my old age. When my strength is gone, do not abandon me.
verses.10: For my enemies have spoken against me, those who watch my life have conspired together,
verses.11: saying, "God has abandoned him. Pursue and seize him, for there is no one to deliver."
verses.12: God, do not be far from me. O my God, come to my rescue, hurry!
verses.13: Let my adversaries be put to shame and brought to nothing. Let those who seek my harm be clothed with disgrace and humiliation.
verses.14: But I will hope always, and add to all your praise.
verses.15: My mouth will declare your righteousness, your salvation all the day, for I do not know how to count them.
verses.16: I will come into the strength of the LORD, LORD, I will remember your righteousness alone.
verses.17: God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I will declare your wonders.
verses.18: Even to old age and gray hair, God, do not abandon me. Until I declare your arm to every generation to come, your strength.
verses.19: And your righteousness, God, reaches to the highest heavens. You have done great things, God. Who is like you?
verses.20: You have shown me many troubles and evils, but you will turn around and bring me to life. From the depths of the earth you will again bring me up.
verses.21: You will abound in your goodness and turn again to comfort me. From the depths you will again bring me up.
verses.22: And I will praise you with the lyre, I will sing your truth, O God, with the harp, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.23: My lips will rejoice as I sing to you, and my soul, which you have redeemed.
verses.24: My tongue will meditate on your righteousness all the day, when those who seek my harm are put to shame and caught in their schemes.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "LORD" is the translation of YHWH. The Hebrew reads "beka YHWH chasiti," which is rendered as "In you, LORD, I have taken refuge."
- v. 6: "from the womb you have been my refuge" reflects the Hebrew phrase "mikev etzba" translated as "from the womb."
- v. 14: "add to all your praise" is a direct rendering of "vehotzifti al kol tehillatecha."
- v. 18: "your strength" reflects the Hebrew "gevuratecha," which is rendered consistently as "strength" or "might."
- v. 24: "caught in their schemes" is a paraphrase of the Hebrew "chaphru," meaning "dug" or "sought in secret," used here in the sense of plotting.
